name: Grupo Supervielle S.A.

profile.description: Grupo Supervielle is an Argentine financial services holding company operating the fourth-largest private domestically-owned bank in Argentina by assets. Founded in 1887, it provides banking, insurance, asset management, and digital financial services through a multi-brand, multi-channel platform. Key subsidiaries include Banco Supervielle, invertirOnline (digital investment platform), and Supervielle Seguros (insurance). Headquartered in Buenos Aires.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Supervielle began a digital transformation in mid-2020 that rebuilt onboarding and credit processes around an Amazon-inspired customer-listening model, and its invertirOnline (IOL) online brokerage has become a growth engine alongside the bank [4]. AI Deployment (1/2): Forbes Argentina reports the bank uses AI to onboard small businesses and grant credit lines fully online within 72 hours, but no quantified AI savings or revenue were disclosed [4]. Market Share (1/2): Supervielle is a meaningful mid-sized private bank serving ~2M active clients through ~130 branches, not a category leader [5]. Pipeline (1/2): 2026 guidance calls for 10-15% real loan growth and management targets ROE approaching 15% in 2027, but product-level launch timelines are vague [2]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No R&D disclosure; technology spend is not separately reported [3].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Founded in 1887 and still led by the Supervielle family, the group articulates a clear customer-centric banking purpose, but it is not distinctive versus Argentine peers. Community Impact (1/2): The group has sat in the BYMA sustainability index (built with the IDB) for multiple years, publishes GRI/SASB-based sustainability reports since 2015, and launched an ESG mutual fund — general rather than distinctive community investment [6]. Employee Retention (0/2): A 2026 rightsizing plan sharply cut headcount, with severance weighing on Q2 2026 results [1][2]. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful net insider buying identified.

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock (forced from portfolios.json) on 6 of 10 weight units because hyperinflation (IAS 29) accounting makes 5-year CAGR and PEG unreliable; weighted sum 2.94/6 = 4.89, rounded to 5. D/E of 84.7% scores 0.94, and FY2025 inflation-adjusted revenue growth of 13.7% (ARS 2.33T vs 2.04T) scores 1.0 [3]. TTM ROE of -4.8% scores 0 at 2x and TTM net margin of -2.4% scores 0, reflecting losses in late 2025 and the AR$12.8B Q2 2026 profit (4.4% ROAE) [1][3]. Forward P/E of ~7.2 is an estimate derived from P/B of ~0.86 and management's 2027 ROE ambition approaching 15% (haircut to ~12%), scoring 1.0 [2][3]. Liquidity cleared: ~568K ADS x $6.97 = ~$4.0M daily.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (5/9): A licensed Argentine bank with a deposit franchise and regulatory moat is not directly replaceable by AI, but its retail and SME lending and IOL brokerage compete with AI-native fintechs and digital wallets that underwrite and service customers at far lower cost — the reason Supervielle is cutting headcount to a 52.3% structural efficiency ratio [1][4]. AI Opportunity (0/1): AI is used in SME onboarding and credit, but no AI-attributable revenue is disclosed [4].

infinite_game.summary: Supervielle's 139-year survival through repeated Argentine crises is genuine endurance, and its 2020 digital push shows adaptation [4]. But the 2026 playbook — deep rightsizing, prioritizing margins over volume and cutting loan-growth guidance — is about restoring near-term ROE rather than advancing a cause [1][2].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): The group's purpose of serving Argentine individuals and SMEs is real but expressed in conventional banking terms; strategy communications center on NIM (20.3% in Q2 2026), cost of risk and ROE targets [1].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): The 2026 rightsizing plan produced a sharp drop in headcount and large severance charges, depressing reported Q2 2026 ROAE to 4.4% vs 14.4% structural — a low-safety environment by Sinek's standard [1][2].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No evidence of rival-as-teacher framing; competitive commentary focuses on margins and market positioning [2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Supervielle has evolved from a traditional bank into a multi-brand group with a digital brokerage, insurance and asset management, but the core remains Argentine commercial banking [4][5].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Leadership launched a full digital transformation in mid-2020 amid a deep Argentine recession and invested in IOL, a costly long-term bet [4]. The 2026 severance-heavy rightsizing is decisive but primarily cost-driven [1].

investment_thesis: Supervielle offers deep-value exposure to Argentine normalization at ~0.86x book: Q2 2026 returned to profit (AR$12.8B, 4.4% ROAE; 14.4% structural ROAE excluding rightsizing effects), NIM expanded to 20.3% from 17.7% as funding costs fell, and the NPL ratio eased to 5.5% [1]. Management targets ROE approaching 15% in 2027 as severance costs roll off and the leaner cost base (52.3% structural efficiency) shows through [2].
thesis_continued: The bear case is that the earnings recovery depends on Argentine macro stability: 2026 reported ROE guidance is only 2-4%, real loan-growth guidance was cut to 10-15%, gross loans fell 1.4% sequentially, and management expects NIM pressure in H2 2026 as corporate assets reprice [1][2]. Cost of risk remains elevated at 5.3-5.8%, ARS devaluation or policy reversal could erase USD returns, and TTM ROE is still negative at -4.8% [2][3].
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results (late November) showing structural ROE progress toward the 2027 ~15% target as severance costs fade [2]
Continued disinflation and lower funding costs in Argentina supporting NIM above the 17-19% guidance range [1][2]
Growth in IOL digital brokerage and dollar-denominated commercial lending [4][5]
key_risks: Argentine macro/political shock (peso devaluation, capital controls, rate spikes) that reverses the normalization thesis
Asset-quality deterioration with NPLs at 5.5% and cost of risk guided at 5.3-5.8% [1][2]
H2 2026 NIM compression as corporate assets reprice, combined with cut loan-growth guidance [2]
